All file operations are confined to `$srcdir` and `$pkgdir`, and the package() function installs from a repacked tarball into the standard node_modules location.

The maintainer demonstrates security awareness by explicitly removing the `.env` file (generated during build with fresh JWT_SECRET/API_KEY_SECRET) from the package, noting it would be world-readable and silently replaced on upgrades. The runtime self-provisions these secrets into `$DATA_DIR` (`~/.omniroute`), making the build-time `.env` pure leakage. No obfuscated code, encoded commands, unexpected network destinations, or system file modifications outside of `$pkgdir` are present. The `npx --yes` usage, while worth noting as it downloads node-gyp from the npm registry, is a legitimate and common practice for native module compilation and does not constitute a security threat.
</details>
